findings.reason: the plan should name `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` as the existing owner of the outstanding-sections derivation and extend or hoist it (as §16 already hoists `section_anchor` into `_plan_html.py`) rather than spell the landing subtraction a second time inside the coverage predicate, which would drift from the owner as the rule changes.
findings.text: the coverage predicate joins the outstanding sections from `roadmap.implementable_sections` (reckon/roadmap.py:107), which selects declared `implementable` sections and does NOT subtract landings, and then applies the landing subtraction itself ("under the landing rule §18 states"); that derivation already exists, module-private, as `promotion._plan_remaining_sections` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:7233), which returns declared implementable sections minus `_landed_sections` (reckon/crew/promotion.py:7210) and is the reader §18 specifically routed through `is_implementable_section` — so §16 forking it re-adds a sixth site of the "which sections are still work" rule that §18 consolidated (comparisons 6→2)

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §16 does not add a module; it hides a whole re-architecture of the fingerprint (section-set digest, third recognised form, span-sliced prose) behind one public function (`strip_tags`), one module-private mapping (`_section_digests`), one module-private coverage predicate and one keyword on an existing public name — an interface far smaller than what it hides.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §16 re-derives the "sections that still have work" set (declared implementable minus landed) that `reckon/crew/promotion.py::_plan_remaining_sections` already owns.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — supplied counts public_definitions 1480, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 adds exactly one public definition (`strip_tags` on `reckon/_plan_html.py`, 1480→1481, matching the supplied base), states why nothing is retired (the identity digest and the prose walk keep their names) and reuses the existing plan-review-missing refusal family, so no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family is added; §20 adds and retires nothing (tests only).
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the design sections search and cite the machinery they extend: the §17 raw-text reader (`structured_section_spans`, `plan_headings`), the tag expression `_TAG_RE` and its consumer `count_open_decisions` in `reckon/_plan_html.py`, the identity trio `section_record_id`/`section_id_candidates`/`is_section_identity`, `roadmap.implementable_sections`, `list_plan_reviews`, `read_plan_review` and `_fingerprint_forms`; §16 names what it moves (`_PROSE_SKIP_TAGS`, `section_anchor`) versus what it keeps, and measures the reuse gap (128 of 151 plans matched, 23 differed).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the design says why the existing machinery is extended rather than wrapped: `strip_tags` is a public function on the module that already owns `_TAG_RE` and does not add a parallel expression (and `count_open_decisions` keeps its bare substitution, with the reason), and §16 argues at length that the coverage predicate is not a wrapper over `read_plan_review` because it joins a section set from one reader to a digest union from another.
